title: State of Maharashtra v. Ramdas Shrinivas Nayak
facts: The case involves a criminal complaint filed by Ramdas Shrinivas Nayak (a former MLA) against the then Chief Minister of Maharashtra, Abdul Rehman Antulay, alleging corrupt practices and misuse of power.
A major issue during High Court revision was whether the Governor must act on his own discretion (individual discretion) when deciding on the sanction for prosecuting a Chief Minister.
During the proceedings, the counsel for the State made a concession regarding the Governor's individual discretion, which was recorded by the High Court judge in the judgment.
The State later challenged this in the Supreme Court, claiming that no such concession was ever made.
issues: Whether the State can challenge a factual recording in a judicial record by a judge (Conclusiveness of Judicial Record).
Whether the Governor acts in his individual discretion while granting sanction under Section 6 of the Prevention of Corruption Act against a Chief Minister.
analysis_of_law: Section 6 of the Prevention of Corruption Act: Necessity of sanction for prosecution.
Article 163 of the Constitution: Exercise of Governor's functions and 'aid and advice' of the Council of Ministers.
Evidence Act: Conclusiveness of judicial proceedings as recorded by the court.
precedent_analysis: The Court emphasized that judges' records of what transpired in court are sacred and can only be set straight by the same court.
Public policy requires that judicial decorum be maintained by not allowing parties to contradict the judge's record.
courts_reasoning: Judicial records are conclusive. If a judge records that a statement was made, it must be believed as final. It's against judicial propriety to launch an inquiry into what happened in the court below.

Regarding the Governor's role: In a situation where a Chief Minister is being prosecuted, the Council of Ministers (his subordinates) would be biased. Therefore, the Governor must act in his 'individual discretion' as a matter of propriety.
The Court held that the State cannot backtrack (resile) from a concession made by its counsel and recorded by the High Court judge.
conclusion: The Supreme Court dismissed the application for special leave to appeal.
The judgment remains a landmark for both judicial record integrity and the Governor's discretionary powers.
full_ratio: Judicial records are conclusive evidence of the proceedings. A statement by a judge in a judgment about what happened in court must be accepted as final. On the Governor's role: when dealing with the prosecution of a Chief Minister, the Governor must act in his own discretion to ensure impartiality.
